title: Optimization Config Apply Benchmark Plan (runtime) — scenarios + thresholds
body:
Purpose
- Validate that versioned Optimization Config apply + rollback does not introduce latency spikes, mixed-worker states, or throughput regressions.
- Provide hard acceptance thresholds to unblock Limited GA (Hosted + Dedicated) and inform default gate settings.
- This is runtime-focused (worker fetch/cache/apply), but includes end-to-end signals needed for safe apply gates.

What we’re benchmarking
A) Apply pipeline behavior
- Fetch + cache config version (control plane → runtime)
- Apply checkpoints (idempotency, retries)
- Partial rollout handling (canary % / shard)
- Rollback path (revert to known-good) and “time to full convergence”

B) Perf impact of optimization changes
- Batching heuristics changes (max batch tokens, prefill/decode split)
- Prefix/KV cache toggles (on/off, invalidation behavior)
- Quantization profile swaps (fp16/bf16 baseline → int8/int4 variants where applicable)

C) Observability correctness
- Metric tags include tenant/model/region/config_version
- Config version annotations show up on dashboards (apply/promote/rollback)

Definitions (for this plan)
- Apply start: rollout controller issues apply to runtime fleet for the target scope
- Converged: ≥ 99% of workers in scope report active_config_version = target within N minutes AND no “mixed active version” for any shard beyond allowed window
- Rollback start: rollback endpoint invoked + accepted
- Rollback complete: ≥ 99% workers in scope back on previous version within N minutes

Test methodology (common)
- Load generator: perf-canary job + internal wrk2-based harness (Sahana coordinating repeatability)
- Traffic profiles: prompt length distributions (short/medium/long), streaming on, tool/function-calling off (unless specified)
- Duration: 10 min warm-up + 30 min steady-state per scenario; capture p50/p95/p99 for prefill and decode separately
- Repeat: 3 runs each (different start times), use median result; flag if run-to-run variance > 8% on p95
- Background: keep GPU util 45–70% for baseline runs; then re-run at 75–85% (saturation sensitivity)
- Error injection: at least one run per apply/rollback scenario with induced control-plane transient errors (HTTP 5xx) and worker restart

Primary metrics collected
- Latency: request p50/p95/p99 (ms), and token-level TTFT (time-to-first-token) for streaming
- Throughput: tokens/sec (aggregate + per GPU), requests/sec
- Reliability: 5xx rate, timeout rate, retry rate, rollback invocation success rate
- Resource: GPU util, GPU memory, CPU, queue depth, batch size distribution
- Apply/rollback: time to converge, number of retries, number of workers stuck, cache invalidation time

Acceptance thresholds (ship / no-ship)
Runtime correctness
- No mixed-version state lasting > 2 minutes for any shard/worker group once apply has entered “progressing”
- Idempotency: re-sending same apply request must not change runtime state beyond first application (no extra invalidations)
- Rollback completes to prior version in <= 5 minutes (P95) for Hosted canary scopes; <= 10 minutes for full region scopes
- On rollback, no sustained 5xx increase > +0.10% absolute for > 5 minutes (transient blips allowed but must self-resolve)

Perf guardrails (relative to baseline on same hardware/model/profile)
- p95 end-to-end latency regression: <= +5% for batching/caching-only changes; <= +8% for quant profile swaps
- p99 latency regression: <= +8% (batch/cache) ; <= +12% (quant)
- TTFT p95 regression: <= +10% (we’ve seen cache invalidation touch TTFT; keep it bounded)
- Throughput: do not regress tokens/sec by more than -3% (batch/cache) or -5% (quant)
- For configs explicitly intended to increase throughput: demonstrate >= +8% tokens/sec at steady-state without exceeding latency guardrails

SLO gate signal quality
- Gate evaluation must be stable enough: < 1 false-positive pause per 10 apply runs under stable load (tracked manually for now)
- All metrics must be emitted with config_version tag within 60s of apply start

Notes / known sensitivities
- Cache invalidation can cause small TTFT spikes (watch for long-tail) — acceptable if bounded and short-lived.
- Quant profile swaps sometimes shift quality; this plan only checks perf + correctness; quality gating is tracked in Applied ML doc.

Scenario matrix (sheet-style)
Legend
- Prompt dist: S=short (p50 128 in / 128 out), M=medium (p50 512 in / 256 out), L=long (p50 2k in / 512 out), XL=context-heavy (p50 6k in / 256 out)
- Concurrency: concurrent streaming requests per replica group (approx)
- Cache: Prefix cache / KV cache
- Batching: “default”, “aggressive”, “conservative” are config presets (we’ll map to actual fields when configs finalize)

Table
scenario_id | env | deployment | model | hw | prompt_dist | max_new_tokens | concurrency | streaming | batching_preset | prefix_cache | kv_cache | quant_profile | rollout | apply_action | expected_risk | success_criteria | notes
S01 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | S | 256 | 64 | on | default | off | on | bf16 | none | baseline | low | establish baseline metrics + variance <8% | baseline used for deltas
S02 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | off | on | bf16 | none | baseline | low | baseline + saturation run at 75–85% GPU | set util via concurrency
S03 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | L | 512 | 64 | on | default | off | on | bf16 | none | baseline | med | baseline for long prompts; watch p99 | queue depth is common confounder
S04 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | XL | 256 | 24 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | none | baseline | high | stable TTFT + no OOMs | validates cache memory behavior
S05 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | aggressive | off | on | bf16 | none | apply(new batching) | med | tokens/sec +8% target AND latency within guardrails | “aggressive” should be throughput win
S06 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | conservative | off | on | bf16 | none | apply(new batching) | low | no worse than -3% throughput; latency improves or flat | sanity for safer preset
S07 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | none | apply(cache on) | med | p95 <= +5%, TTFT <= +10%, cache hit rate > 0.35 after warm-up | requires repeated prefixes in load
S08 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | canary10% | safe_apply(canary) | med | canary progresses; no mixed-version >2m; gate signals present | tests rollout controller hooks
S09 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | canary10% | rollback(canary) | high | rollback <=5m P95; transient errors bounded; workers converge | exercise hot rollback path
S10 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | L | 512 | 64 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | canary25% | safe_apply(canary) | high | p99 within guardrails; no OOMs; gate stable | longest prompts + cache is tail-risk
S11 | staging | Dedicated | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 96 | on | default | off | on | bf16 | canary10% | safe_apply(canary) | med | same as Hosted, plus isolation scope correctness | ensure tenant scoping tags
S12 | staging | Dedicated | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 96 | on | default | off | on | bf16 | full | promote(full) | med | converge <=10m; no mixed-version >2m; no 5xx spike | full-scope apply
S13 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | off | on | int8 | canary10% | apply(quant swap) | high | latency within quant guardrails; tokens/sec no worse than -5% | perf only; quality handled elsewhere
S14 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | off | on | int8 | canary10% | rollback(quant swap) | high | rollback <=5m; post-rollback metrics return within 3% of bf16 baseline | verify “restores baseline”
S15 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-13b | L40Sx8 | S | 256 | 256 | on | aggressive | on | on | bf16 | canary10% | apply(cache+batch) | med | no p95 regression >5%; throughput +8% | lower-end GPU sensitivity
S16 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-13b | L40Sx8 | M | 256 | 192 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | canary10% | rollback(cache+batch) | med | rollback <=5m; TTFT spike <10% and <3m | focus on cache invalidation behavior
S17 | staging | Hosted | rw-mistral-7b | A10x8 | S | 256 | 384 | on | default | off | on | bf16 | canary25% | apply(batching) | low | ensure tags correct + no regressions | “cheap” coverage for lots of runs
S18 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | canary10% | apply w/ injected control-plane 5xx | high | retries succeed; no stuck workers; converge <=10m | simulate transient failures
S19 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | canary10% | apply + worker restarts | high | state recovers; no mixed-version >2m after restarts | validates checkpointing
S20 | staging | Hosted | rw-llama-70b | H100x8 | M | 256 | 128 | on | default | on | on | bf16 | canary10% | concurrent apply+rollback race | highest | must end in consistent version (rollback wins) + audit events emitted | reproduce prior race condition

Data to record per run (copy/paste checklist)
- config_version_from → to (include hash/id)
- scope (tenant/model/region) and rollout type (canary%, full)
- start/end timestamps (apply start, first metrics tagged, converge time)
- dashboard links (latency/5xx/throughput) and annotation presence
- any runtime logs with “apply checkpoint” and retries
- result summary: pass/fail + which threshold violated

Open questions (as of 2026-01-08)
- Do we want different converge-time thresholds for multi-region apply vs single region? (SRE leaning yes; need Sean/Allison input)
- For cache invalidation: can we make TTFT guardrail tighter if we add gradual invalidation? (Noah investigating)
- Quant swap: should we separate TTFT and steady-state decode latency thresholds? (feels like yes; keep simple for now)

Owners / next steps
- Sofia: finalize scenario presets mapping to actual Optimization Config fields once schema stabilizes (post-ENG-4822)
- Omar: implement “repeated prefix” load profile for cache hit-rate scenarios (S07/S10)
- Allison: confirm dashboards produce per-config_version breakdown + annotations (needed for gate debugging)
- Sahana: make runs deterministic + reduce flake; produce run template for CI/e2e (ties into ENG-4830)

Changelog
- 2025-11-06: initial draft scenarios (batching + cache)
- 2025-12-12: added canary + rollback convergence metrics
- 2026-01-08: added race scenario S20 and explicit acceptance thresholds for mixed-version window
